source.method: Visual review of the locked V40 printed step 5 panel, rendered privately; no source pixels are copied into authored output
source.observation: The two motors sit between the rear flanges of Plate A with their output shafts passing outward through the large flange holes. Two M3x25 screws per motor enter from the outside through the small flange holes and the gearbox; a spring washer and an M3 nut thread on from the inside, arrows pointing outward. The motor cans point toward the rear and the motor wires face inward.

placement.shaft: The motor shaft axis is the axis of the large (12 mm) flange hole; the shaft leaves the gearbox on the outer side and passes through the flange.
placement.gearbox: The gearbox face that carries the shaft is flush with the flange face on the chassis-centre side.
placement.canDirection: Toward the rear (installed -X). This is the only direction in which the flange's two small holes, 21 mm behind the shaft hole, pass through the gearbox body; the V40 panel shows the same direction.
placement.stackOrderAlongScrew: screw head on the outer flange face, flange, gearbox, spring washer, nut (accepted ordered stack)
placement.screwToHole: Screws 001 and 003 use the first small hole (smaller flange-local v), screws 002 and 004 the second; 001/002 belong to the robot-LEFT motor and 003/004 to the RIGHT motor

approach.motorTravel: Diagonal: outward along the shaft and up (unit of 0, outward, +1). The exploded start is below and inboard so the can clears the central rear wall; only the start pose is checked, no path is claimed.
approach.note: Nonphysical exploded staging only. Washers and nuts arrive from the chassis-centre side, the screws from outside.

limitations: The motor proxy has no mounting bores or thread detail: each screw passes through the gearbox as a declared omitted-bore proxy overlap bounded by the screw's own shank volume, not an engagement or fit
The motor's two mounting-hole positions are not modelled; the gearbox is placed from its output shaft and flange face, and screw paths are taken from the traced Plate A flange holes
Plate A flange hole positions are photo-traced approximations; the 2 mm thickness is probable, not measured
Motor wires and leads are zero-solid schematic and are not routed; no electrical, torque or retention claim
Spring washer opening roll and nut hex roll about the screw axis are deterministic presentation gauges, not measured orientations
